chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Joe Barufaldi and other bandsmen who went on or left music
summary: Barufaldi is still playing; a great pianist in the band took the GI Bill to Harvard and became a lawyer; Davison would like to forget the Army.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Now, was Joe Barufaldi in that band?
And, was he the only one that went on to play in the fairly well known---
Well, he is still going strong---
around - he is still playing in New York. He plays with bands like at the Roseland.
Oh, sure. And, then he goes down with Billy Maxted in Florida - quite often, but I got him back; I got him out of -- he lived at Plymouth, Rhode Island - or is it Plymouth--
Yeah - where the Mayflower landed - up there---

Yeah and I got him to come to New York - I said, listen, the way you play you could - you know - he was with me on a couple of my small bands around New York for awhile. I put him in the band. He was a very good player and still is---
Was there anybody else in that Army band that went on into music? Or, is he the only one?

Well they should have but they didn't. I had one of the greatest piano players I ever heard and he always wanted to go to Harvard and, of course, you know when the guys got out of the Army at that point, they gave you---
GI Bill took you into any college you wanted to go. But, he went to Harvard and became a lawyer and wound up working for the State Department in Washington. And, such things like that.
And, you can't remember his name, right?
But, that's a long, long time ago. It's one part of my life I sure would like to forget--
